text:
Justin Barron was claimed off waivers from Nashville in late September and arrived in St. Louis as depth. Sixteen games later he has three goals and 10 points, is playing 16:39 a night (up from 14:15 last season), and the New York Times' headline caught the mood: "Blues newcomer Justin Barron is cooking but remains modest."

How much is real? More than you'd think. Our form check calls it earned: nine points in his last ten against 3.8 expected at his ice time, with more chances of his own (1.1 expected goals against 0.8 usual). With him on the ice at five on five, the Blues have taken 55.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 7.8 points better than without him. His speed shows up too: 20 bursts over 20 mph, 90th percentile.

Some of it will cool. His points rate is well above the top of our talent range, and his shooting is running at 12%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags the weak spot: only 30% of his exits kept possession last season. Still, a former first-rounder on his fourth team has found a real role.
headline: Justin Barron, waiver claim, is cooking in St. Louis
